binaries.name: mke2fs
binaries.why: create_inode is linked into it in this build, which is where the overwrite lives

binaries.name: libext2fs
binaries.why: it owns fs->now, the inode write primitives and the superblock stamping

evidenceStandard.why: the same standard the frozen binary's walk was held to, so the two reads are comparable evidence

paths.failCondition: a load from the stat buffer's st_ctime reaching a store into the inode buffer's i_ctime, which is what the frozen binary does
paths.passCondition: no instruction writes i_ctime from the staged file's st_ctime; the field must come from fs->now or be left as ext2fs_write_new_inode set it
paths.what: the inode mke2fs -d writes for a regular file copied from the staging tree

paths.failCondition: a wall-clock call reaching these stamps when fs->now is set
paths.passCondition: these still take fs->now, so the candidate does not regress the path the fixed time already handles
paths.what: the inodes mke2fs creates itself, including the root and lost+found, and the superblock stamps

acceptanceCriteria.why: The frozen binary's defect was established by reading it. A candidate accepted on observed output would be accepted on a sample rather than on the code path.

conditionsCarriedIntoThisRecord: Do not assume a newer version fixed it; statically read the actual candidate binary.
Check both the i_ctime of a staged regular file inode and the inodes and superblock mke2fs creates itself.
Confirm both mke2fs and libext2fs use the fixed time.
Allow only candidates whose official origin, signature, version and sha256 are verifiable; no forks and no local patches.
Pre-register candidate, origin, size, verification method and the source-lock addition method on a remote branch before downloading.
Do not modify the existing 191-package source lock or any sealed record; add to a successor only.
approval.grantedFor: identifying and verifying an official candidate, then adding it to a successor source lock
approval.option: Pin an official e2fsprogs whose create_inode honours fs->now.

recordsThatStayByteUnchanged.sealedBySubject: native-shadow: seal the arm64 root-disk determinism hard stop and its cause (#253)
native-shadow: pin the sealed boot records by digest (#255)
native-shadow: seal ARM64 boot rootfs source lock over verified payloads (#239)

howResolved: Reconstructed the frozen Ubuntu archive keyring from the digest-pinned ubuntu-keyring deb and confirmed both the deb and the extracted keyring against the digests the existing lock already pins.
Fetched each candidate suite's InRelease and verified its signature with that keyring using gpgv.
Took the Packages index digest from the signed InRelease body and checked the fetched index against it.
Read the e2fsprogs and libext2fs2t64 stanzas from the verified index.
order: Fetch and verify the candidate suite's InRelease against the frozen Ubuntu keyring.
Fetch the Packages index the verified InRelease pins and check its digest.
Read the e2fsprogs and libext2fs stanzas and record version, size and sha256 here.
Push this record with those values.
Only then fetch the debs and check each against the recorded sha256.
candidateDiscovery.whyEmpty: Empty at pre-registration and filled here from signature-verified indexes. No deb has been fetched at the time this list was written.

candidateFamily.origin: Ubuntu archive snapshots served from snapshot.ubuntu.com, the same origin the existing 191-package lock already uses
candidateFamily.searchOrder: Ubuntu suites later than noble, in ascending release order, taking the e2fsprogs and libext2fs binary packages that suite publishes.
candidateFamily.whyThisOrigin: Its trust chain is already frozen and verified in this repository, so a candidate needs no new trust root.

defect.howTheTwoSetsWereSeparated: In the sealed run the fixed time was the no-op value 0, so every stamp fell back to the wall clock and all seven fields moved. Only i_ctime is written from the staged file's stat, so it is the only one a non-zero fixed time leaves moving.
defect.site: mke2fs create_inode set_inode_extra, which runs after ext2fs_write_new_inode and overwrites the times it wrote
defect.whyTheFrozenBinaryCannotBeMadeDeterminis: i_ctime is copied from the staging file's st_ctime, and st_ctime cannot be set from userspace by any caller. E2FSPROGS_FAKE_TIME=1 fixes every other stamp because those go through fs->now, which is why it is necessary but not sufficient. No environment value, staging order or builder flag reaches the field, so the fix has to be a different binary.

deferredToTheOperator.why: Both were excluded by the approval. If a hard stop is reached they are the operator's call, not this record's.

hardStopConditions.meaning: no official e2fsprogs build reachable through this trust chain removes the staged-ctime write
a candidate was read and still writes i_ctime from the staged file's st_ctime
the candidate's origin, signature, version or digest cannot be established
the candidate binary cannot be read to the evidence standard recorded here

preRegistration.why: A criterion written after seeing the candidate is not a criterion. The accept/reject rule, the trust chain and the stop conditions are fixed in the remote before anything is fetched.

productionReadiness.note: A passing read unblocks exactly one production of two arm64 replicas, on the terms the successor authority record already fixed.

sourceLockAdditionMethod.fullRehashOfTheExistingPackages: once, immediately before the successor lock is sealed, and not before
sourceLockAdditionMethod.how: A successor lock record binds the existing lock by digest and adds only the candidate packages. The 191 entries are reused from the content-addressed store without a network request.

steps.how: the archive signing keyring already frozen in the source lock, matched by digest
the candidate suite's InRelease, signature checked against that keyring
steps.note: the pinned digest is noble's; a candidate suite has its own InRelease, verified the same way against the same keyring

steps.how: the Packages index digest as pinned by the verified InRelease
steps.note: as above, the candidate suite's own index is verified through its own InRelease

steps.how: the package stanza digest from the verified index, then the downloaded file's sha256
